# Bounded automatic genetic FA-rank contract

Status: design frozen for future implementation review, 2026-10-01. No automatic selector is implemented or validated by this document. The current fixed-rank Gaussian FA route remains experimental, and public covered count stays seven. Approved scope and execution record: [design arc](auto-fa-rank-design-plan-20261001.md).

## Model and candidates

The first selector is explicit opt-in and compares only shared genetic factor counts `K={0,1}` for four complete Gaussian traits, pedigree relationships, one record per observed animal, trait intercepts and an unstructured residual covariance. The same records, labels, units, X, Z and Ainv are used for both candidates. Explicit fixed-rank calls keep their current meaning; omission of rank does not invoke selection. Missing responses, other trait counts/ranks, other fixed effects, genomic/custom relationships, repeatability and non-Gaussian models are refused before fitting. K=2 is outside this design.

Write `Y=XB+ZU+E`. For the engine's record-major order, `y=vec(Y')`, `u=vec(U')`, `X_full=X⊗I_4`, `Z_full=Z⊗I_4`,

`Cov(u)=A⊗G_K`, `Cov(vec(E'))=I_n⊗R`,

`V_K=Z_full(A⊗G_K)Z_full'+I_n⊗R`,

`G_K=L_K L_K'+diag(psi)`, `psi_i=c+exp(theta_i)`, `c=1e-4` in squared units of trait i.

| Candidate | Shape and future implementation mapping | Genetic parameters |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| K=0 | Diagonal G with positive trait-specific genetic variances. Selector-internal floor-matched diagonal fit; no loading columns. | 4 |
| K=1 | Existing FA shape with four loadings and four positive uniquenesses; rank-one shared component. | 8 |

K measures shared factors, not the rank of G, which is positive definite when uniquenesses are positive. K=0 still permits genetic variance. Zero genetic signal is a separate boundary case, outside the fitted strictly-positive family.

The existing public diagonal route uses `exp(theta)` without c, while FA uses `c+exp(theta)`. A direct call to the current diagonal fitter is therefore not a floor-matched nested comparator. Future implementation must add the matched internal candidate without changing the public fixed-rank diagonal route, the FA rank guard or the existing floor. It must retain ten identical residual log-Cholesky coordinates in both candidates. Exact source findings: [engine review](../dev-log/scout/2026-10-01-auto-fa-rank-design/engine-contract.md), `src/multivariate.jl:660-723,844-856,1010-1055` at base `28f90e09`.

Identifiability is a property of the covariance and record design. With one record per animal, Z=I and A=I, only G+R is identifiable. That design is refused for automatic selection; its likelihood is retained as a deterministic negative witness. The identification screen must compare genetic and residual kernels on the REML contrast space: use Q with Q'X_full=0 and inspect Q'V_K Q, not raw A versus I alone. Exact or numerically unresolved proportional kernels on that space must refuse selection with a design-identification reason. For intercept-only one-record data, the informative-looking half-sib matrix A=(1-rho)I+rho*11' becomes (1-rho)I after removing the intercept direction; G and R remain confounded. This is a second deterministic refusal witness. Relatedness alone does not establish good finite-sample information. The future pre-run must freeze a numerical kernel-rank check and its unit convention before real selection fits; no numerical conditioning threshold is claimed validated here.

For general K the nominal genetic dimension is `4K-K(K-1)/2+4`. At K=2 it exceeds the ten-dimensional ambient symmetric G space. This dimension screen does not prove identifiability at K=1. At L=0 the derivative of LL' is zero; diagonal-to-FA nesting is singular, so the score below is not a regular four-df likelihood-ratio test.

## Criterion and numerical comparison

Freeze criterion name `reml_aic_covariance` as an experimental comparison rule on the common fixed-effect contrast space:

`C_K=-2*ell_REML,K+2*q_K`, `q_K=q_G(K)+q_R`, `q_R=10`.

The exact engine REML normalization is

`ell_REML=-0.5*((4n-p_full)*log(2*pi)+logdet(V)+logdet(X_full' V^-1 X_full)+y'P y)`,

`P=V^-1-V^-1 X_full (X_full'V^-1 X_full)^-1 X_full'V^-1`, `p_full=4`.

The four common fixed intercepts are removed by REML and not counted in q. The displayed q values are 14 and 18; penalties are 28 and 36. Counting common intercepts in both penalties would shift scores equally but is not this declared convention. Residual parameters are counted and displayed even though they cancel in the difference.

Define signed difference `D=C_1-C_0=8-2*(ell_1-ell_0)`. Negative D favors K=1. Away from numerical ties, K=1 wins when `2*(ell_1-ell_0)>8`. Report both full C values and D; calculate D directly from the likelihood difference to reduce cancellation. Reevaluate both objectives on the identical input model before ranking.

Freeze numerical tie band `tau=1e-6` criterion units for the initial moderate-scale validation cell. Require each returned loglik to agree with independent same-covariance reevaluation within `1e-8` absolute loglik units before selection. Thus the two objective discrepancies can contribute at most `4e-8` to D under this check, below tau; this discrepancy budget is a check convention, not a proof of all floating-point or optimizer error. If the future pre-run cannot meet it, stop and revise the numerical contract before any campaign. Do not enlarge it after seeing selected ranks.

If `abs(D)<=tau`, choose K=0 and set `near_tie=true`; an exact tie is included. If D is below -tau choose K=1; otherwise choose K=0. Return tau and the objective discrepancies. This band handles numerical ambiguity; it is not an evidence-strength cutoff or a calibrated confidence interval. Weak substantive separation remains visible as the raw D, even when outside tau.

This is a restricted-likelihood covariance comparison with nominal parameter penalties and a singular smaller model. It does not establish consistency, correct biological dimension, marginal predictive optimality or calibrated rank probabilities. Gurka discusses ambiguities in REML model selection; the chosen bounded rule needs its own selection study. [Gurka (2006)](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1198/000313006X90396).

The mixed-model selection review motivates keeping the likelihood target, covariance boundaries and effective sample size explicit. [Müller, Scealy and Welsh (2013)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.2427). BIC is deferred because no pedigree-specific effective sample-size rule has been justified. [Delattre, Lavielle and Poursat (2014)](https://doi.org/10.1214/14-EJS890). The singular boundary also prevents treating D as an ordinary chi-square test. [Self and Liang (1987)](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1987.10478472). These sources motivate limits; none validates this exact selector.

Marginal ML-AIC would require a genuinely fitted ML objective for both candidates. Evaluating ML only at REML estimates is excluded. Conditional AIC, BIC, rank probabilities and automatic criterion switching are outside this first contract.

## Starts, eligibility and failure policy

Fit the floor-matched diagonal candidate from the documented phenotype-based default; fit FA from its existing default and balanced starts. Neither uses generating truth. Permit at most one additional FA retry, only when the initial FA candidate is failed, unconverged or materially non-nested relative to the eligible diagonal candidate, or when a better finite unconverged FA attempt exceeds the best eligible converged FA loglik by more than tau/2. Thus the first budget is one diagonal optimizer start and at most three FA starts, four total. The unequal budget is declared; it does not imply equal optimization robustness.

The additional FA start uses the diagonal covariance as a target with a deterministic, nonzero loading perturbation and corresponding floor-safe uniquenesses, preserving the covariance as closely as feasible. The implementation must write the exact initializer and verify it before fitting. A zero-loading start is excluded because its first-order loading gradient vanishes. No extra retries, changed data, changed floor or hidden warm starts are allowed. Retain the initial attempt even if the retry succeeds.

Each candidate uses its best eligible converged start within this budget. Eligibility requires finite objective and estimates, positive-definite G and R, the shared floor constraint, convergence, matched inputs/normalization and successful objective reevaluation. A better finite unconverged start exceeding the chosen converged loglik by `tau/2` makes selection unavailable after the one allowed retry. Start covariance disagreement and objective ranges remain visible; they do not certify a global optimum.

With a matched floor, the FA family contains the diagonal covariance at L=0. If the best eligible FA loglik remains below the diagonal loglik by more than `tau/2`, flag a nesting/optimization failure and refuse selection. The nested witness is an objective evaluation at L=0, not a successful FA optimization claim.

All tau/2 comparisons above use loglik units because tau is defined in criterion units. Both candidate ranks must be eligible to select a rank. If either fails after its budget, return `selection_status=unavailable`, no selected rank/fit, a reason and all attempts. A sole successful candidate does not win by default. The user may request an explicit fixed rank independently; no silent fallback fit is made.

Near-floor candidates can remain eligible under the experimental score, with `boundary_sensitive=true`. The floor flag is defined for both candidates because both now share c. It is not a claim of uniqueness identification. At or numerically below the bound is an admissibility failure. The fixed absolute floor is unit-dependent; no silent standardization, rescaling or new preprocessing is introduced. Unit-change validation must identify where selection changes because constraints change.

hs_validate_auto_fa_rank_control <- function(control, target, spec, payload) {
  rank_selection <- hs_engine_control_value(control, "rank_selection", NULL)
  if (is.null(rank_selection)) return(FALSE)
  if (!is.character(rank_selection) || length(rank_selection) != 1L ||
      is.na(rank_selection) || !identical(rank_selection, "auto")) {
    hs_abort_unsupported_syntax(
      "`engine_control$rank_selection` currently accepts only `\"auto\"`."
    )
  }
  if (!identical(control$engine, "julia") || !identical(target, "multivariate") ||
      !"target" %in% names(control$engine_control)) {
    hs_abort_unsupported_syntax(
      "Automatic FA-rank selection requires explicit `engine = \"julia\"` and `target = \"multivariate\"`."
    )
  }
  hs_validate_iterations(hs_engine_control_value(control, "iterations", 2000L))
  conflicts <- intersect(
    names(control$engine_control), c("rank", "initial", "genetic_structure")
  )
  if (length(conflicts)) {
    hs_abort_unsupported_syntax(
      "`rank_selection = \"auto\"` cannot be combined with explicit ",
      paste(sprintf("`%s`", conflicts), collapse = ", "), "."
    )
  }
  if (!isTRUE(spec$response$multivariate) || !is.matrix(payload$Y) ||
      ncol(payload$Y) != 4L || anyNA(payload$Y) ||
      !identical(payload$family, "gaussian") ||
      !identical(spec$method, "REML") ||
      !identical(names(spec$random), "animal") ||
      ncol(payload$X) != 1L ||
      !identical(payload$metadata$fixed_colnames, "(Intercept)") ||
      nrow(payload$Z) != nrow(payload$Y) ||
      any(Matrix::rowSums(payload$Z != 0) != 1) ||
      any(Matrix::colSums(payload$Z != 0) > 1)) {
    hs_abort_unsupported_syntax(
      "Automatic FA-rank selection currently requires four complete Gaussian traits, ",
      "a pedigree `animal()` effect, trait intercepts only, and one record per observed animal."
    )
  }
  TRUE
}

hs_fa_rank_scalar <- function(row, name, type) {
  value <- row[[name]]
  if (is.null(value) || length(value) == 0L) {
    return(switch(type, numeric = NA_real_, integer = NA_integer_, logical = NA, character = NA_character_))
  }
  if (is.character(value) && identical(value[[1L]], "__HSQ_NONE__")) {
    return(switch(type, numeric = NA_real_, integer = NA_integer_, logical = NA, character = NA_character_))
  }
  switch(type,
    numeric = as.numeric(value[[1L]]),
    integer = as.integer(value[[1L]]),
    logical = as.logical(value[[1L]]),
    character = as.character(value[[1L]])
  )
}

hs_fa_decode_vector <- function(value) {
  if (is.null(value) || length(value) == 0L) return(NULL)
  if (!is.character(value) || is.na(value[[1L]])) return(as.numeric(value))
  encoded <- value[[1L]]
  if (identical(encoded, "__HSQ_NONE__")) return(NULL)
  if (!nzchar(encoded)) return(numeric())
  as.numeric(strsplit(encoded, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]])
}

hs_fa_decode_matrix <- function(value) {
  if (is.null(value) || length(value) == 0L) return(NULL)
  if (!is.character(value) || is.na(value[[1L]])) return(value)
  encoded <- value[[1L]]
  if (identical(encoded, "__HSQ_NONE__")) return(NULL)
  dimensions_text <- sub(":.*$", "", encoded)
  dimensions <- as.integer(strsplit(dimensions_text, "x", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]])
  if (length(dimensions) != 2L || anyNA(dimensions)) {
    stop("Internal bridge error: encoded selector matrix has invalid dimensions.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  values_text <- sub("^[^:]*:", "", encoded)
  values <- if (nzchar(values_text)) as.numeric(strsplit(values_text, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]) else numeric()
  if (length(values) != prod(dimensions)) {
    stop("Internal bridge error: encoded selector matrix has invalid value count.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  matrix(values, nrow = dimensions[[1L]], ncol = dimensions[[2L]])
}

# Shared production interrupt boundary. The runner and reader are private
# injection seams for the controlled Julia->R interruption witness.
hs_julia_run_fa_rank_command <- function(
  command, ledger_name,
  runner = JuliaCall::julia_command,
  ledger_reader = function() JuliaCall::julia_eval(paste0(ledger_name, "[]"))
) {
  propagate_interrupt <- function(err) {
    partial <- tryCatch(ledger_reader(), error = function(ignore) NULL)
    condition <- structure(
      list(message = conditionMessage(err), call = conditionCall(err), partial_ledger = partial),
      class = c("hsquared_fa_rank_interrupt", "interrupt", "condition")
    )
    stop(condition)
  }
  tryCatch(
    runner(command),
    interrupt = propagate_interrupt,
    error = function(err) {
      is_interrupt <- inherits(err, "interrupt") || inherits(err, "hsquared_julia_interrupt") ||
        grepl("InterruptException|interrupted", conditionMessage(err), ignore.case = TRUE)
      if (is_interrupt) propagate_interrupt(err)
      stop(err)
    }
  )
}

hs_fa_rank_rows <- function(rows, schema) {
  fields <- names(schema)
  if (is.null(rows)) rows <- list()
  if (is.data.frame(rows)) rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(rows)), function(i) as.list(rows[i, , drop = FALSE]))
  if (is.list(rows) && length(rows) && !is.null(names(rows)) && all(fields %in% names(rows))) {
    n_rows <- length(rows[[fields[[1L]]]])
    column_cell <- function(column, i, type) {
      if (type == "matrix") {
        if (is.character(column)) return(hs_fa_decode_matrix(column[[i]]))
        dimensions <- dim(column)
        if (length(dimensions) == 3L && dimensions[[3L]] == n_rows) {
          return(column[, , i])
        }
        if (is.list(column) && length(column) == n_rows) return(column[[i]])
        if (n_rows == 1L && length(dimensions) == 2L) return(column)
        if (is.null(column) && n_rows == 1L) return(NULL)
        stop("Internal bridge error: selector covariance column lost row/matrix dimensions.", call. = FALSE)
      }
      if (type == "vector") {
        if (is.character(column)) return(hs_fa_decode_vector(column[[i]]))
        if (is.list(column) && length(column) == n_rows) return(column[[i]])
        if (is.matrix(column) && nrow(column) == n_rows) return(as.numeric(column[i, ]))
        if (is.matrix(column) && ncol(column) == n_rows) return(as.numeric(column[, i]))
        if (is.list(column) && n_rows == 1L) return(column[[1L]])
        if (is.null(column) && n_rows == 1L) return(NULL)
        stop("Internal bridge error: selector vector column lost row dimensions.", call. = FALSE)
      }
      if (is.list(column)) column[[i]] else column[[i]]
    }
    rows <- lapply(seq_len(n_rows), function(i) {
      stats::setNames(lapply(fields, function(field) {
        column_cell(rows[[field]], i, schema[[field]])
      }), fields)
    })
  }
  if (!is.list(rows)) stop("Internal bridge error: selector rows are not a list.", call. = FALSE)
  out <- lapply(fields, function(field) {
    type <- schema[[field]]
    if (type %in% c("matrix", "vector")) {
      I(lapply(rows, function(row) row[[field]]))
    } else {
      vapply(rows, hs_fa_rank_scalar, FUN.VALUE = switch(type,
        numeric = NA_real_, integer = NA_integer_, logical = NA, character = NA_character_
      ), name = field, type = type)
    }
  })
  names(out) <- fields
  as.data.frame(out, optional = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
}

hs_normalize_fa_rank_selection <- function(
  raw, payload, selected_fit = NULL, spec = NULL, call = NULL
) {
  if (is.environment(raw)) raw <- as.list(raw)
  get <- function(name, default = NULL) raw[[name]] %||% default
  candidate_schema <- list(
    rank = "integer", structure = "character", status = "character", reason = "character",
    eligible = "logical", selected_start = "character", loglik = "numeric", q = "integer",
    penalty = "numeric", criterion = "numeric", converged = "logical", attempts_count = "integer",
    minimum_floor_distance = "numeric", near_floor = "logical", objective_range = "numeric",
    g_relative_disagreement = "numeric", r_relative_disagreement = "numeric"
  )
  attempt_schema <- list(
    rank = "integer", structure = "character", start_id = "character", retry_index = "integer",
    attempted = "logical", status = "character", reason = "character", converged = "logical", optimizer_status = "character",
    optimizer_iterations = "integer", optimizer_objective = "numeric",
    finite_objective = "logical", finite_estimates = "logical",
    pd_genetic = "logical", pd_residual = "logical", loglik = "numeric", reevaluated_loglik = "numeric",
    objective_discrepancy = "numeric", q = "integer", penalty = "numeric", criterion = "numeric",
    initial_parameters = "vector", estimated_parameters = "vector",
    uniqueness = "vector", floor_distances = "vector", near_floor = "logical", eligible = "logical",
    selected_within_rank = "logical", selected = "logical", genetic_covariance = "matrix",
    residual_covariance = "matrix", genetic_loadings = "matrix"
  )
  candidate_summary <- hs_fa_rank_rows(get("candidate_summary"), candidate_schema)
  attempts <- hs_fa_rank_rows(get("attempts"), attempt_schema)
  if (nrow(candidate_summary) != 2L) {
    stop("Internal bridge error: FA selector must return both candidate rows.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  status <- as.character(get("selection_status", "unavailable"))[[1L]]
  selected <- NULL
  if (identical(status, "selected")) {
    if (is.null(selected_fit)) selected_fit <- get("selected_fit")
    if (is.null(selected_fit)) stop("Internal bridge error: selected rank lacks its fit payload.", call. = FALSE)
    result <- hs_normalize_multivariate_result(
      selected_fit, payload, allow_missing_fa_start_metadata = TRUE
    )
    selected_spec <- spec %||% list(
      method = "REML", family = list(family = "gaussian", link = "identity"),
      target = "multivariate"
    )
    selected <- hs_new_fit(
      call = call,
      spec = selected_spec,
      payload = payload, result = result, engine = "HSquared.jl"
    )
  }
  structure(list(
    selection_status = status,
    reason = hs_fa_rank_scalar(list(reason = get("reason")), "reason", "character"),
    requested_ranks = c(0L, 1L), selected_rank = hs_fa_rank_scalar(list(x = get("selected_rank")), "x", "integer"),
    criterion = as.character(get("criterion", "reml_aic_covariance"))[[1L]],
    criterion_status = as.character(get("criterion_status", "experimental"))[[1L]],
    q = get("q", c(14L, 18L)), penalties = get("penalties", c(28, 36)),
    criterion_difference = hs_fa_rank_scalar(list(x = get("criterion_difference")), "x", "numeric"),
    tie_tolerance = hs_fa_rank_scalar(list(x = get("tie_tolerance")), "x", "numeric"),
    near_tie = hs_fa_rank_scalar(list(x = get("near_tie")), "x", "logical"),
    kernel_ratio = hs_fa_rank_scalar(list(x = get("kernel_ratio")), "x", "numeric"),
    nesting_witness_discrepancy = hs_fa_rank_scalar(
      list(x = get("nesting_witness_discrepancy")), "x", "numeric"
    ),
    candidate_summary = candidate_summary, attempts = attempts,
    records = get("records"), design_fingerprint = get("design_fingerprint"),
    relationship_fingerprint = get("relationship_fingerprint"),
    boundary_sensitive = hs_fa_rank_scalar(list(x = get("boundary_sensitive")), "x", "logical"),
    start_sensitive = hs_fa_rank_scalar(list(x = get("start_sensitive")), "x", "logical"),
    uncertainty_scope = as.character(get("uncertainty_scope", "conditional_on_selected_rank"))[[1L]],
    selected_fit = selected
  ), class = "hsquared_fa_rank_selection")
}

#' @export
print.hsquared_fa_rank_selection <- function(x, ...) {
  cat("<hsquared_fa_rank_selection>\n")
  cat("  status: ", x$selection_status, "\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(x$selected_rank) && !is.na(x$selected_rank)) cat("  selected shared-factor count: ", x$selected_rank, "\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(x$reason) && !is.na(x$reason)) cat("  reason: ", x$reason, "\n", sep = "")

# Normalized Legendre basis row vector phi(t) = [phi_0(t), ..., phi_{k-1}(t)] at a
# standardized covariate t in [-1, 1], mirroring `HSquared.legendre_basis`:
# phi_n(t) = sqrt((2n+1)/2) * P_n(t), with P_n the ordinary Legendre polynomials
# via the Bonnet recurrence. Used by the R-side reaction-norm trajectory
# extractors so they need no live Julia round-trip. Errors -- does not
# clamp -- for |t| > 1 + 1e-10, matching the Julia engine's tolerance exactly
# (#213); within that tolerance t is clamped to [-1, 1] before use, as Julia
# also does.
hs_legendre_basis <- function(t, order) {
  order <- as.integer(order)
  t <- as.numeric(t)
  if (t < -1 - 1e-10 || t > 1 + 1e-10) {
    hs_abort_out_of_range(
      "`t` must be in [-1, 1]; standardize the covariate first ",
      "(see `hs_standardize_covariate()`), got t = ",
      format(t, trim = TRUE),
      "."
    )
  }
  tt <- max(-1, min(1, t))
  p <- numeric(order)
  p[1L] <- 1
  if (order >= 2L) {
    p[2L] <- tt
  }
  if (order >= 3L) {
    for (n in 2:(order - 1L)) {
      p[n + 1L] <- ((2 * n - 1) * tt * p[n] - (n - 1) * p[n - 1L]) / n
    }
  }
  phi <- numeric(order)
  for (n in 0:(order - 1L)) {
    phi[n + 1L] <- sqrt((2 * n + 1) / 2) * p[n + 1L]
  }
  phi
}

# n x order normalized-Legendre design over already-standardized points `ts`,
# mirroring `HSquared.legendre_design`. Errors via `hs_legendre_basis()` if any
# `ts` point is outside [-1 - 1e-10, 1 + 1e-10].
hs_legendre_design <- function(ts, order) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(ts, hs_legendre_basis, order = order))
}

# Map a raw covariate value/vector onto t in [-1, 1] using the recorded fit
# range, mirroring `HSquared.standardize_covariate`
# (t = 2(a - lower)/(upper - lower) - 1).
hs_standardize_covariate <- function(a, lower, upper) {
  2 * (as.numeric(a) - lower) / (upper - lower) - 1
}

hs_unstandardize_covariate <- function(t, lower, upper) {
  lower + (as.numeric(t) + 1) * (upper - lower) / 2
}

hs_validate_two_effect_initial <- function(initial) {
  if (
    !is.numeric(initial) ||
      !setequal(names(initial), c("sigma_a2", "sigma_c2", "sigma_e2"))
  ) {
    stop(
      "`initial` for the two-effect target must be a named numeric vector ",
      "with `sigma_a2`, `sigma_c2`, and `sigma_e2`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  if (any(!is.finite(initial)) || any(initial <= 0)) {
    stop(
      "`initial` variance components must be finite and positive.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  initial[c("sigma_a2", "sigma_c2", "sigma_e2")]
}

# Opt-in, experimental genomic GREML estimator. Surfaces the Julia-owned
# `HSquared.fit_ai_reml()` REML optimizer on an animal_model_spec built with the
# user-supplied genomic relationship inverse `Ginv` (in place of a pedigree
# Ainv). Reuses the standard result normalizer, relabelling the genetic
# component as "genomic".
hs_fit_julia_genomic_payload <- function(
  payload,
  project = hs_default_julia_project(),
  initial = c(sigma_a2 = 1, sigma_e2 = 1),
  iterations = 100L
) {
  if (!inherits(payload, "hs_bridge_payload")) {
    stop("`payload` must be an internal `hs_bridge_payload`.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  from_markers <- identical(payload$relationship_source, "markers")
  if (is.null(payload$Ginv) && !from_markers) {
    stop(
      "Internal bridge error: the genomic payload is missing its `Ginv`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  if (from_markers && is.null(payload$markers)) {
    stop(
      "Internal bridge error: the genomic payload is missing its `markers`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  if (!hs_julia_bridge_available(project)) {
    stop(
      "The experimental Julia bridge requires Julia, the `JuliaCall` R ",
      "package, and a local `HSquared.jl` project.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  initial <- hs_validate_initial_variances(initial)
  iterations <- hs_validate_iterations(iterations)
  hs_julia_setup(project)
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_y", payload$y)
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_X", payload$X)
  hs_julia_assign_sparse_csc("hsq_Z", payload$Z)
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_ids", payload$ids)
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_initial_sigma_a2", unname(initial[["sigma_a2"]]))
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_initial_sigma_e2", unname(initial[["sigma_e2"]]))
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_iterations", iterations)
  if (from_markers) {
    # Build the frozen sample-p VanRaden-1 relationship and its regularized
    # precision in Julia. The engine owns the canonical construction metadata
    # and SHA-256 provenance fingerprints; R carries them unchanged.
    JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_markers", payload$markers)
    JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_ridge", payload$ridge)
    if (is.null(payload$marker_names)) {
      marker_names_cmd <- "hsq_marker_names = nothing;"
    } else {
      JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_marker_names", payload$marker_names)
      marker_names_cmd <- ""
    }
    relinv_cmd <- paste(
      marker_names_cmd,
      "hsq_genomic_construction =",
      "HSquared._genomic_activation_construction(",
      "hsq_markers, hsq_ids; marker_names = hsq_marker_names,",
      "ridge = hsq_ridge);",
      "hsq_Ginvs = sparse(hsq_genomic_construction.Q);",
      "hsq_genomic_provenance = hsq_genomic_construction.provenance;",
      "hsq_genomic_kernel = hsq_genomic_construction.K;"
    )
  } else {
    JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_Ginv", payload$Ginv)
    relinv_cmd <- if (identical(payload$relationship, "genomic")) {
      paste(
        "hsq_Ginvs = sparse(hsq_Ginv);",
        "hsq_genomic_provenance =",
        "HSquared._genomic_precision_provenance(hsq_Ginv, hsq_ids);",
        "hsq_genomic_kernel = nothing;"
      )
    } else {
      paste(
        "hsq_Ginvs = sparse(hsq_Ginv);",
        "hsq_genomic_provenance = nothing;",
        "hsq_genomic_kernel = nothing;"
      )
    }
  }
  rel <- payload$relationship
  boundary_eligible <- identical(rel, "genomic") &&
    nrow(payload$Z) == ncol(payload$Z) &&
    nrow(payload$Z) <= 2000L &&
    isTRUE(all.equal(
      as.matrix(payload$Z),
      diag(nrow(payload$Z)),
      tolerance = 1e-12,
      check.attributes = FALSE
    ))
  fit_cmd <- if (boundary_eligible) {
    paste(
      "hsq_boundary_result = HSquared._fit_ai_reml_genomic_boundary(",
      "hsq_spec;",
      "provenance = hsq_genomic_provenance,",
      "kernel = hsq_genomic_kernel,",
      "initial = (sigma_a2 = hsq_initial_sigma_a2,",
      "sigma_e2 = hsq_initial_sigma_e2),",
      "iterations = hsq_iterations);",
      "hsq_fit = hsq_boundary_result.fit;"
    )
  } else {
    paste(
      "hsq_boundary_result = nothing;",
      "hsq_fit = HSquared.fit_ai_reml(",
      "hsq_spec;",
      "initial = (sigma_a2 = hsq_initial_sigma_a2,",
#' Create hsquared control options
#'
#' `hs_control()` records execution and storage controls for hsquared model
#' calls. The default `engine = "fit"` fits the validated v0.1 Gaussian
#' animal model through the `HSquared.jl` engine (average-information REML);
#' `engine = "validate"` parses and validates the contract without fitting,
#' returning the validated spec invisibly; and `engine = "julia"` exposes
#' advanced engine controls.
#'
#' @param engine Execution engine. `"fit"` (default) fits the v0.1 Gaussian
#'   animal model via the `HSquared.jl` engine; this requires a local Julia,
#'   the `JuliaCall` package, and an `HSquared.jl` checkout. `"validate"`
#'   validates the parser and bridge payload without fitting, then returns the
#'   validated spec invisibly (after a confirming message). `"julia"` exposes
#'   the advanced opt-in bridge with explicit `target` control.
#' @param backend Planned compute backend. One of `"auto"`, `"cpu"`,
#'   `"threads"`, `"cuda"`, `"amdgpu"`, `"metal"`, or `"oneapi"`.
#' @param accelerator Planned accelerator preference. One of `"auto"`,
#'   `"none"`, `"gpu"`, `"cuda"`, `"amdgpu"`, `"metal"`, or `"oneapi"`.
#' @param precision Planned numeric precision. One of `"float64"` or
#'   `"float32"`.
#' @param save Planned fitted-object storage mode. One of `"minimal"`,
#'   `"full"`, or `"tiny"`.
#' @param engine_control A named list for engine-specific controls. The current
#'   experimental Julia bridge recognizes `julia_project`, `initial`,
#'   `iterations`, `em_warmup`, `target`, `variance_components`, `marginal`,
#'   `max_dense_cells`, `scale_method`, `genetic_structure`, `rank`,
#'   `rank_selection`, and
#'   `experimental_gllvm`.
#'   `julia_project` is honoured by every `target`; supplying a key a given
#'   `target` does not honour errors (hsquared#212) rather than being
#'   silently ignored. Per-target honoured keys (besides `julia_project`):
#'   * `fit_animal_model` (default): `initial`, `max_dense_cells`.
#'   * `henderson_mme`, `metafounder`, `snp_blup`: `variance_components`.
#'   * `ai_reml`: `initial`, `iterations`, `em_warmup`.
#'   * `sparse_reml`, `two_effect`, `direct_maternal`,
#'     `genomic`, `single_step`, `single_step_construct`,
#'     `metafounder_single_step`, `relmat`, `precision`: `initial`,
#'     `iterations`.
#'   * `repeatability`: `initial`, `iterations`, `max_dense_cells`,
#'     `scale_method`.
#'   * `multi_effect`: `initial`, `iterations`, `scale_method`. Both the
#'     default dense route and the opt-in `scale_method = "auto"` route
#'     forward `initial` and `iterations` to the Julia fitter.
#'   * `multivariate`: `initial`, `iterations`, `genetic_structure`, `rank`,
#'     `rank_selection`.
#'   * `genetic_gllvm`: `iterations`, `genetic_structure`, `rank`,
#'     `experimental_gllvm` (`initial` is not exposed on this route).
#'   * `multivariate_repeatability`: `initial`, `iterations`.
#'   * `random_regression`: `iterations` (no `initial`).
#'   * `nongaussian`: `marginal`, `iterations`, `initial` (a list with
#'     `sigma_a2`), `restart_check`.
#'   `max_dense_cells` bounds `nobs^2 + nanimals^2` on
#'   the engine's dense-validation fitters (hsquared#214, #217): the default Julia
#'   target `target = "fit_animal_model"` (via `HSquared.fit_animal_model()` /
#'   `fit_variance_components()`) and `target = "repeatability"`. Both require
#'   `engine = "julia"`. It has **no effect** under the default `engine = "fit"`
#'   path, which routes to the sparse-capable `HSquared.fit_ai_reml()` and enforces
#'   no dense-cell cap at all. It must be a
#'   single positive integer; the default, `1e6`, mirrors the engine's own
#'   `DEFAULT_MAX_DENSE_CELLS` unchanged. Raise it to fit a larger dense
#'   problem at the cost of memory and time, or switch to a sparse route
#'   (`target = "ai_reml"`/`"sparse_reml"`) instead of raising it indefinitely.
#'   Exceeding the cap now raises an `hsquared_error` naming the observed cell
#'   count and the effective cap, rather than a raw Julia trace.
#'   On `target = "repeatability"`, `max_dense_cells` reaches the point fit only.
#'   The opt-in repeatability-coefficient interval is computed by a separate engine
#'   entry point that exposes no such control and runs at the engine default
#'   (`1e6`), so **raising the cap above `1e6` returns the point fit with the
#'   interval silently absent** (`NULL`) rather than with an error. Tracked on the
#'   engine side; not fixed here. This applies to `scale_method = "dense"` only:
#'   the sparse route forms its interval from the fitted components and never
#'   reaches that entry point, so it is unaffected by `max_dense_cells`.
#'
#'   `target` selects which Julia estimator the `engine = "julia"` bridge runs;
#'   it has no effect under the default `engine = "fit"` path. The supported
#'   targets are `"fit_animal_model"`, `"ai_reml"`, `"sparse_reml"`,
#'   `"henderson_mme"`, `"repeatability"`, `"two_effect"`, `"multi_effect"`,
#'   `"direct_maternal"`, `"random_regression"`, `"genomic"`,
#'   `"single_step"`, `"single_step_construct"`, `"metafounder"`,
#'   `"metafounder_single_step"`, `"snp_blup"`, `"relmat"`, `"precision"`,
#'   `"multivariate"`, `"multivariate_repeatability"`, `"nongaussian"`, and
#'   `"genetic_gllvm"`,
#'   described below. Covered opt-in
#'   routes (validation scale; not the default path) include `"two_effect"`
#'   (`common_env()`), `"direct_maternal"`, `"multi_effect"`, and
#'   `"random_regression"` at `k = 2`. `marginal` applies only to
#'   `target = "nongaussian"`.
#'   With `engine = "julia"` and no `target`, the bridge defaults to
#'   `target = "fit_animal_model"`: it surfaces the Julia-owned
#'   `HSquared.fit_animal_model()` dense NelderMead optimizer, honouring the
#'   `REML` flag. This is **not** the same estimator as the default
#'   `engine = "fit"` path, which runs the validated average-information REML
#'   estimator (`HSquared.fit_ai_reml()`, the same one reached by
#'   `target = "ai_reml"`). The two paths target the same Gaussian animal model
#'   but differ at the optimizer level, so their estimates can differ slightly.
#'   Reach the validated estimator with `engine = "fit"` (the ordinary path) or
#'   with `engine = "julia"` and `target = "ai_reml"`.
#'   `target = "henderson_mme"` is a supplied-variance validation path and
#'   requires `variance_components` with named `sigma_a2` and `sigma_e2` values.
#'   `target = "metafounder"` is an experimental supplied-variance validation
#'   path for `metafounder(1 | id, pedigree = ped, group = mf_group, Gamma =
#'   Gamma)`. It builds the Julia-owned animal-only `A^Gamma` relationship;
#'   `Gamma` and the variance components are supplied, not estimated.
#'   `target = "sparse_reml"` is an experimental, opt-in validation path that
#'   surfaces the Julia-owned `HSquared.fit_sparse_reml()` REML-only sparse
#'   optimizer; it accepts `initial` (named `sigma_a2`/`sigma_e2`) and
#'   `iterations`. It is not the default, not production fitting, and not a
#'   variance-component estimation claim for the public R interface.
#'   `target = "ai_reml"` exposes the same average-information REML estimator
#'   (`HSquared.fit_ai_reml()`) that the default `engine = "fit"` path uses,
#'   with explicit `initial` and `iterations` control. This is the validated
#'   v0.1 estimator for the univariate Gaussian animal model; the `engine = "fit"`
#'   default is the ordinary way to reach it. `em_warmup` (a non-negative integer,
#'   default `0`) optionally runs that many EM-REML warm-start steps before the
#'   average-information iterations; it applies to this estimator on both the
#'   default `engine = "fit"` path and `target = "ai_reml"`. `em_warmup = 0` (the
#'   default) is byte-identical to the previous behaviour. A small positive value
#'   (e.g. `3`) can rescue convergence from poor starting variances; on an
#'   identified fit it converges to the same optimum.
#'   `target = "repeatability"` is an experimental, opt-in path for the
#'   repeatability (permanent-environment) model. It requires
#'   `animal(1 | id, pedigree = ped) + permanent(1 | id)` in the formula and
#'   surfaces the Julia-owned `HSquared.fit_repeatability_reml()` REML-only
#'   optimizer (three-component `initial` with `sigma_a2`/`sigma_pe2`/`sigma_e2`).
#'   It is REML only, not the default, and the additive and permanent-environment
#'   variances are identifiable only with repeated records per individual.
#'   `scale_method` selects the estimator. `"dense"` (the default) is the
#'   covered validation-scale `fit_repeatability_reml()` above, which the engine
#'   refuses once `nobs^2 + nanimals^2` exceeds `max_dense_cells` -- a ceiling
#'   any field-scale repeated-measures pedigree passes easily.
#'   `scale_method = "auto"` fits the SAME model through the engine's sparse
#'   K-effect AI-REML (`fit_multi_effect(method = :auto)`), expressing it as the
#'   animal block plus an identity-relationship permanent-environment block, and
#'   so has no dense ceiling. Below the ceiling the two agree to REML tolerance.
#'   Two differences are deliberate on the sparse route: `initial` and
#'   `iterations` are NOT honoured (the engine picks its own; a supplied value
#'   warns), and `loglik` carries the REML normalising constant
#'   `-(n - p)/2 * log(2 * pi)` that the dense route omits -- so
#'   log-likelihoods, AIC, or likelihood-ratio tests must NOT be compared
#'   across `scale_method` on the raw `loglik` (HSquared.jl #365). Fit

hs_julia_fa_rank_partial_ledger_command <- function(ledger_name) {
  paste(
    hs_julia_fa_rank_rows_serialization_command(),
    paste0("hsq_fa_interrupt_snapshot = ", ledger_name, "[];"),
    "hsq_fa_interrupt_raw = hsq_fa_interrupt_snapshot === nothing ? nothing : Dict(String(k) => getfield(hsq_fa_interrupt_snapshot, k) for k in keys(hsq_fa_interrupt_snapshot));",
    "if hsq_fa_interrupt_snapshot !== nothing;",
    "for key in keys(hsq_fa_interrupt_raw); value = hsq_fa_interrupt_raw[key]; value === nothing && (hsq_fa_interrupt_raw[key] = \"__HSQ_NONE__\"); value isa Symbol && (hsq_fa_interrupt_raw[key] = string(value)); end;",
    "hsq_fa_interrupt_raw[\"selection_status\"] = string(hsq_fa_interrupt_snapshot.selection_status);",
    "hsq_fa_interrupt_raw[\"criterion\"] = string(hsq_fa_interrupt_snapshot.criterion);",
    "hsq_fa_interrupt_raw[\"criterion_status\"] = string(hsq_fa_interrupt_snapshot.criterion_status);",
    "hsq_fa_interrupt_raw[\"uncertainty_scope\"] = string(hsq_fa_interrupt_snapshot.uncertainty_scope);",
    "hsq_fa_interrupt_raw[\"reason\"] = hsq_fa_interrupt_snapshot.reason === nothing ? \"__HSQ_NONE__\" : string(hsq_fa_interrupt_snapshot.reason);",
    "hsq_fa_interrupt_raw[\"candidate_summary\"] = hsq_selection_rows(hsq_fa_interrupt_snapshot.candidate_summary);",
    "hsq_fa_interrupt_raw[\"attempts\"] = hsq_selection_rows(hsq_fa_interrupt_snapshot.attempts);",
    "end;"
  )
}

hs_julia_read_fa_rank_partial_ledger <- function(ledger_name, payload) {
  JuliaCall::julia_command(hs_julia_fa_rank_partial_ledger_command(ledger_name))
  raw <- JuliaCall::julia_eval("hsq_fa_interrupt_raw")
  if (is.null(raw)) return(NULL)
  if (is.environment(raw)) raw <- as.list(raw)
  for (field in names(raw)) {
    if (identical(raw[[field]], "__HSQ_NONE__")) raw[[field]] <- NULL
  }
  hs_normalize_fa_rank_selection(raw, payload)
}

hs_fit_julia_fa_rank_selection_payload <- function(
  payload, project = hs_default_julia_project(), iterations = 2000L,
  spec = NULL, call = NULL
) {
  if (!inherits(payload, "hs_bridge_payload") || is.null(payload$pedigree)) {
    stop("Automatic FA-rank selection requires a validated pedigree bridge payload.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  iterations <- hs_validate_iterations(iterations)
  hs_julia_setup(project)
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_Y", hs_y_matrix_for_julia(payload$Y))
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_X", payload$X)
  hs_julia_assign_sparse_csc("hsq_Z", payload$Z)
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_mv_ids", as.character(payload$ids))
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_id", payload$pedigree$id)
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_sire", hs_parent_for_julia(payload$pedigree$sire))
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_dam", hs_parent_for_julia(payload$pedigree$dam))
  traits <- payload$metadata$trait_names %||% colnames(payload$Y) %||% paste0("trait", seq_len(ncol(payload$Y)))
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_traits", as.character(traits))
  JuliaCall::julia_assign("hsq_iterations", iterations)
  ledger_name <- paste0(
    "hsq_fa_ledger_",
    gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", basename(tempfile("request_")))
  )
  JuliaCall::julia_command(paste0(ledger_name, " = Ref{Any}(nothing);"))
  on.exit(
    try(JuliaCall::julia_command(paste0(ledger_name, "[] = nothing;")), silent = TRUE),
    add = TRUE
  )

  command <- paste(
    "hsq_ped = HSquared.normalize_pedigree(hsq_id, hsq_sire, hsq_dam);",
    "string.(hsq_ped.ids) == hsq_mv_ids || error(\"FA selector pedigree ID order changed across bridge\");",
    "hsq_selection = HSquared.select_fa_rank(hsq_Y, hsq_X, hsq_Z, hsq_ped;",
    "ids = hsq_ped.ids, traits = hsq_traits, iterations = hsq_iterations, ledger_sink = ", ledger_name, ");"
  )
  hs_julia_run_fa_rank_command(
    paste(command, hs_julia_fa_rank_serialization_command()), ledger_name,
    ledger_reader = function() hs_julia_read_fa_rank_partial_ledger(ledger_name, payload)
  )
  raw <- JuliaCall::julia_eval("hsq_selection_raw")
  hs_normalize_fa_rank_selection(raw, payload, spec = spec, call = call)
}

test_that("automatic FA-rank control is explicit and rejects conflicting or unsupported routes", {
  spec <- list(method = "REML", response = list(multivariate = TRUE), random = list(animal = TRUE))
  payload <- list(
    Y = matrix(1, 5, 4), X = matrix(1, 5, 1), Z = diag(5),
    family = "gaussian",
    metadata = list(fixed_colnames = "(Intercept)")
  )
  control <- hs_control(engine = "julia", engine_control = list(
    target = "multivariate", rank_selection = "auto"
  ))
  expect_true(hsquared:::hs_validate_auto_fa_rank_control(control, "multivariate", spec, payload))

  fixed_rank <- hs_control(engine = "julia", engine_control = list(
    target = "multivariate", genetic_structure = "factor_analytic", rank = 1L
  ))
  expect_false(hsquared:::hs_validate_auto_fa_rank_control(
    fixed_rank, "multivariate", spec, payload
  ))

  conflict <- hs_control(engine = "julia", engine_control = list(
    target = "multivariate", rank_selection = "auto", rank = 1L
  ))
  expect_error(
    hsquared:::hs_validate_auto_fa_rank_control(conflict, "multivariate", spec, payload),
    class = "hsquared_unsupported_syntax"
  )
  non_julia <- hs_control(engine = "fit", engine_control = list(
    target = "multivariate", rank_selection = "auto"
  ))
  expect_error(
    hsquared:::hs_validate_auto_fa_rank_control(non_julia, "multivariate", spec, payload),
    class = "hsquared_unsupported_syntax"
  )
  non_reml <- spec
  non_reml$method <- "ML"
  expect_error(
    hsquared:::hs_validate_auto_fa_rank_control(control, "multivariate", non_reml, payload),
    class = "hsquared_unsupported_syntax"
  )
  incomplete <- payload
  incomplete$Y[1, 1] <- NA_real_
  expect_error(
    hsquared:::hs_validate_auto_fa_rank_control(control, "multivariate", spec, incomplete),
    class = "hsquared_unsupported_syntax"
  )
  non_gaussian <- payload
  non_gaussian$family <- "poisson"
  expect_error(
    hsquared:::hs_validate_auto_fa_rank_control(control, "multivariate", spec, non_gaussian),
    class = "hsquared_unsupported_syntax"
  )
  repeated <- payload
  repeated$Z[2, ] <- repeated$Z[1, ]
  expect_error(
    hsquared:::hs_validate_auto_fa_rank_control(control, "multivariate", spec, repeated),
    class = "hsquared_unsupported_syntax"
  )
  three_traits <- payload
  three_traits$Y <- three_traits$Y[, 1:3, drop = FALSE]
  expect_error(
    hsquared:::hs_validate_auto_fa_rank_control(control, "multivariate", spec, three_traits),
    class = "hsquared_unsupported_syntax"
  )
})

  relinv_primary <- spec$random$genomic
  if (is.null(relinv_primary)) {
    relinv_primary <- spec$random$single_step
  }
  # Experimental supplied-relationship primary effects (`relmat()`/`precision()`)
  # carry the same supplied-inverse spec shape as genomic's `Ginv`, so they reuse
  # the supplied-relationship-inverse payload path unchanged.
  if (is.null(relinv_primary)) {
    relinv_primary <- spec$random$relmat
  }
  if (is.null(relinv_primary)) {
    relinv_primary <- spec$random$precision
  }
  if (!is.null(relinv_primary)) {
    return(hs_build_relinv_bridge_payload(spec, relinv_primary))
  }

  animal <- spec$random$animal
  is_metafounder <- FALSE
  if (is.null(animal)) {
    animal <- spec$random$metafounder
    is_metafounder <- TRUE
  }
  pedigree <- animal$pedigree
  observed_ids <- animal$values
  ids <- pedigree$ids
  id_index <- match(observed_ids, ids)

  if (anyNA(id_index)) {
    stop(
      "Internal bridge error: observed animal IDs are not aligned with the ",
      "validated pedigree.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  Z <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(
    i = seq_along(id_index),
    j = id_index,
    x = 1,
    dims = c(length(id_index), length(ids)),
    dimnames = list(NULL, ids)
  )

  # Second design matrix `Z2` for the opt-in two-effect model: a record incidence
  # on the second effect's levels. `common_env` levels are the environmental
  # groups with an identity relationship; `maternal_genetic` levels are the
  # pedigree animals (dams expressed through `Z2`) with the pedigree relationship.
  Z2 <- NULL
  effect2 <- NULL
  second <- spec$random$common_env
  if (is.null(second)) {
    second <- spec$random$maternal_genetic
  }
  if (!is.null(second)) {
    levels2 <- second$levels
    index2 <- match(second$values, levels2)
    Z2 <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(
      i = seq_along(index2),
      j = index2,
      x = 1,
      dims = c(length(index2), length(levels2)),
      dimnames = list(NULL, levels2)
    )
    effect2 <- list(
      type = second$type,
      group = second$group,
      levels = levels2,
      relationship = second$relationship
    )
  }

  # Opt-in random-regression (reaction-norm) design carried on `animal()`'s LHS:
  # the per-record covariate and the number of Legendre coefficients travel in
  # the payload; the engine builds the n x k Phi basis from the standardized
  # covariate. The recorded (lower, upper) bounds let extractors re-standardize a
  # user-supplied `at =` covariate value on the original scale.
  rr <- animal$random_regression

  # Payload-v2: an ordered list of random-effect blocks. The existing top-level
  # Z / Z2 / effect2 fields are preserved byte-for-byte (back-compat alias section 4 of
  # the frozen schema 21-payload-v2-multiblock-schema.md). The `random_effects`
  # list is ADDITIVE; the v0.1 dispatch in julia-bridge.R is unchanged.
  pedigree_rows <- list(
    id = pedigree$data$id,
    sire = pedigree$data$sire,
    dam = pedigree$data$dam,
    sire_index = pedigree$parent_index$sire,
    dam_index = pedigree$parent_index$dam,
    original_order = pedigree$original_order
  )
  block1 <- list(
    name = "animal",
    type = "pedigree",
    Z = Z,
    relmat_inverse = NULL,
    relmat_status = "build_in_julia",
    pedigree = pedigree_rows,
    ids = ids
  )
  random_effects <- if (is.null(effect2)) {
    # v0.1: single pedigree block only
    list(block1)
  } else {
    second_type <- effect2$relationship
    # `second$type` encodes "common_env", "maternal_genetic" (from model-spec.R)
    block2_name <- switch(
      effect2$type,
      common_env = "common_env",
      maternal_genetic = "maternal",
      effect2$type # fallback: preserve the raw type
    )
    block2_type <- if (identical(second_type, "identity")) "iid" else "pedigree"
    block2 <- list(
      name = block2_name,
      type = block2_type,
      Z = Z2,
      relmat_inverse = NULL,
      relmat_status = if (identical(second_type, "identity")) {
        "identity"
      } else {
        "build_in_julia"
      },
      pedigree = if (identical(block2_type, "pedigree")) {
        pedigree_rows
      } else {
        NULL
      },
      ids = effect2$levels
    )

  }

  # Detect it via spec$random$permanent and append a third block if present.
  permanent <- spec$random$permanent
  if (!is.null(permanent)) {
    perm_ids <- unique(as.character(permanent$values))
    block_perm <- list(
      name = "permanent",
      type = "iid",
      Z = Z,
      relmat_inverse = NULL,
      relmat_status = "identity",
      relmat_status = "identity",
      pedigree = NULL,
      ids = perm_ids
    )
    random_effects <- c(random_effects, list(block_perm))
  }

  # Arbitrary-N bare `(1 | group)` i.i.d. random effects (opt-in multi-effect
  # model). Each becomes an independent identity-relationship block: a record
  # incidence `Z_i` on the group's levels, `relmat_status = "identity"` (the
  # engine builds `sparse(I, q_i, q_i)`), and no pedigree. The Julia parser routes

  # `fit_multi_effect_reml`.
  iid_effects <- spec$random$iid_effects

      index_i <- match(eff$values, levels_i)
      Zi <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(

        j = index_i,
        x = 1,
        dims = c(length(index_i), length(levels_i)),
        dimnames = list(NULL, levels_i)
      )
      block_iid <- list(
        name = eff$group,
        type = "iid",
        Z = Zi,
        relmat_inverse = NULL,
        relmat_status = "identity",
        pedigree = NULL,
        ids = levels_i
      )
      random_effects <- c(random_effects, list(block_iid))
    }
  }

  structure(
    list(
      payload_version = 2L,
      y = if (isTRUE(spec$response$multivariate)) {
        NULL
      } else {
        as.numeric(spec$response$values)
      },
      Y = if (isTRUE(spec$response$multivariate)) {
        unname(as.matrix(spec$response$values))
      } else {
        NULL
      },
      X = unname(as.matrix(spec$fixed$design)),
      Z = Z,
      Z2 = Z2,
      effect2 = effect2,
      random_effects = random_effects,
      random_regression = rr,
      Ainv = NULL,
      group_of = if (is_metafounder) animal$group_of else NULL,
      Gamma = if (is_metafounder) animal$Gamma else NULL,
      gamma_labels = if (is_metafounder) animal$gamma_labels else NULL,
      relationship_source = if (is_metafounder) "metafounder" else "pedigree",
      method = spec$method,
      family = spec$family$family,
      # Per-record trial counts (a vector, possibly varying across records) for a
      # cbind(successes, failures) binomial response; NULL for every other
      # response (Bernoulli/Poisson/Gaussian).
      n_trials = spec$response$n_trials,
      ids = ids,
      pedigree = list(
        id = pedigree$data$id,
        sire = pedigree$data$sire,
        dam = pedigree$data$dam,
        sire_index = pedigree$parent_index$sire,
        dam_index = pedigree$parent_index$dam,
        original_order = pedigree$original_order
      ),
      metadata = list(
        response = spec$response$name,
        response_type = if (isTRUE(spec$response$multivariate)) {
          "multivariate"
        } else if (!is.null(rr)) {
          "random_regression"
        } else {
          "univariate"
        },
        trait_names = spec$response$trait_names,
        random_regression = if (is.null(rr)) {
          NULL
        } else {

            order = rr$order,
            lower = rr$lower,
            upper = rr$upper
          )
        },
        fixed_colnames = colnames(spec$fixed$design),

        observed_id_index = id_index,
        relationship = animal$relationship,
        gamma_source = if (is_metafounder) "supplied" else NULL,
        fixed_terms = spec$fixed$terms,
        contrasts = spec$fixed$contrasts,
        ainv_status = "build_in_julia",
        ainv_target = paste0(
          "HSquared.pedigree_inverse(",
          "HSquared.normalize_pedigree(id, sire, dam))"

        julia_spec_target = paste0(

          } else {
            paste0(

              "ids = ids, method = :",
              spec$method,
              ")"
            )
          }
        ),
        julia_fit_target = paste0("HSquared.", spec$bridge$target)
      )
    ),
    class = c("hs_bridge_payload", "list")
  )
}
